topics.title: DNA Repair Pathways
topics.productionRationale: NHEJ, HR, NER, BER, MMR — five mechanisms, five disease associations (BRCA, XP, HNPCC). Dense mechanism topic.

topics.title: Metabolic Fuel Use & Starvation
topics.productionRationale: Fuel-source timeline (2-sec phosphocreatine → days 1–3 gluconeogenesis → post-day-3 ketone-dominant brain shift) — the integration endpoint of all metabolism topics.

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: Fuel-source dominance across duration of exercise
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: Fig 7: % maximal energy by source (y, 0 to 100%) vs duration of exercise (x: 2 sec, 10 sec, 1 min, 2 hr) — five curves with legend: stored ATP (starts 100%, spent within seconds), creatine phosphate (peaks between 2 and 10 sec), anaerobic metabolism (peaks near 1 min), aerobic metabolism (rises continuously, dominant after ~1 min), overall performance (100% at start, flat to ~10 sec, declines to low plateau by 2 hr).

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: Stored energy decline across weeks of starvation
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: Fig 8: stored energy (kJ) (y, ticks 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 0) vs weeks of starvation (x, 0-8) — three solid curves: protein (starts 12, slow decline accelerating after week 6 to ~5 at week 8), fat (starts 12, near-linear decline to ~1 at week 8), carbohydrate (starts ~0.5, at zero within week 1). Invisible text-layer artifacts present (duplicated right-axis '100% / % Maximal energy by source', stray '2 sec') — InDesign leftovers, not visible in print.

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: The states table: priorities banner (supply sufficient glucose to the brain and RBCs and preserve protein); fed state (glycolysis + aerobic respiration; insulin stores TG/glycogen + protein synthesis); fasting (hepatic glycogenolysis major, GNG + adipose FFA minor; glucagon/epinephrine); starvation days 1-3 (glycogenolysis, adipose FFA, glucose-to-FFA shift, GNG from lactate/alanine/glycerol/propionyl-CoA from odd-chain FFA; glycogen depleted after day 1; RBCs lack mitochondria); starvation after day 3 (adipose stores, ketones main brain source; depleted stores → vital protein degradation → organ failure and death; excess stores determine survival time).

visualPlan.rightsPosture: All First Aid 2026 artwork is COPYRIGHTED_NO_REPUBLISH — no republish license exists. Every educationally meaningful visual therefore receives an ORIGINAL_KYP_REDRAW or ORIGINAL_KYP_ADAPTATION (registry SVG or note-block); SOURCE_REFERENCE is used only for visuals genuinely absorbed by another note (receiving location named) or duplicated.
visualPlan.diagnosticPatternPolicy: Clinical photographs, histology, radiology and cytogenetics visuals are implemented as KYP originals that preserve the diagnostic pattern (e.g., cherry-red macula contrast, dark-peripheral heterochromatin on EM, dextrocardia silhouette position, crumpled-tissue-paper cytoplasm) — never superficial redraws.

notes: Phase I-C full extraction. 54 new topics (status pending) + 1 approved pilot note. Topic granularity follows the approved pilot pattern (teachable units spanning 1–6 FA subsections; subsection coverage recorded per topic in faSubsections — every FA subsection on pdf 54–114 is claimed by exactly one topic). textbookVisuals[] is the pre-production visual source inventory; at production time records transfer into content/usmle/visual-inventory/<topicId>.json with kypVisualId and qaStatus filled. Cross-topic visuals absorbed by the pilot note are SOURCE_REFERENCE with the receiving note named. Production proceeds batch-by-batch per contract §9.2; no topic may silently disappear.
